back: A long-term change (decades or more) in the average climate, such as rising temperature or shifting rainfall.
Gases absorb outgoing long-wave heat and re-radiate some back, keeping the Earth about 15 °C on average instead of about −18 °C.
Extra warming from greenhouse gases added by human activities.
Temperature records, ice cores, Arctic sea ice, retreating glaciers, sea-level rise, historical and natural records.
About 280 ppm before industrialisation; over 400 ppm today (approximate).
Changes in orbit shape (~100,000 years), tilt (~41,000 years) and wobble (~20,000-26,000 years); explain ice ages.
Sulphur droplets reflect sunlight: global cooling for 1-3 years (e.g. Pinatubo 1991).
Fossil fuels and cement (CO₂), deforestation (CO₂), cattle, rice and landfills (methane), fertilisers (nitrous oxide).
Urban heat islands, dams (humidity), deforestation and desertification (hotter, drier), afforestation (cooler).
